questions.q: Which of these does the chapter list as something a retreat CAN do?
options: Guarantee that you will feel God's presence
Interrupt a pattern and help you name what you are carrying
Replace medical or psychological care
Fix in three days what took years to form
questions.explanation: A retreat can interrupt a pattern, give unhurried honesty before God, help you name what you carry, restore perspective and begin things. The other three are in the 'cannot' list.

questions.q: What point does the chapter draw from Luke the physician (Colossians 4:14) and Paul's advice to Timothy (1 Timothy 5:23)?
options: Doctors are unnecessary for people of faith
Scripture does not force a choice between depending on God and receiving appropriate care through ordinary means
Only physical illness deserves treatment
Prayer should replace medicine
questions.explanation: Prayer and silence may support healing and form part of wider care, but they are not substitutes for medical or psychological treatment.

questions.q: Why does the chapter say a retreat cannot make a difficult decision for you?
options: Because decisions should be made by your pastor
Because a strong feeling during a retreat is not the same as divine instruction; impressions must be tested against Scripture, wise counsel and existing responsibilities
Because God never speaks during retreats
Because decisions require a group vote
questions.explanation: Treating a feeling as instruction has led sincere people into serious mistakes. Part Five walks through testing what you believe you heard.

questions.q: What is the chapter's guidance on forgiveness for readers with abuse in their past?
options: Forgiveness requires reconciliation and renewed contact
Forgiveness must be completed by the end of Session Six
Forgiveness is real but is not the same as reconciliation, trust or returning to danger; it does not require contact and is not on a schedule
Forgiveness is impossible in such cases
questions.explanation: Forgiveness does not remove the need for truth, boundaries, justice, reporting or consequences, and you are never required to put yourself back within reach of someone who harmed you.

questions.q: If a session brings up more than you can hold, what is the chapter's simple rule?
options: Push through; discomfort means it is working
Stop the session, not necessarily the retreat: stand up, go outside, orient to the present, contact your support person
Abandon the whole retreat and go home immediately
Fast until the feeling passes
questions.explanation: The sessions are offered, not assigned. A paused retreat is not a failed one; Elijah slept and ate twice before God spoke to him.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four paths the chapter asks you to choose from before beginning?
options: Proceed independently
Proceed with support
Use an adapted format
Proceed without telling anyone
questions.explanation: The fourth path is to postpone for now and seek professional, medical, crisis or safety support first. Postponing is not failing; it may be the wisest way to prepare.

reflection: After reading this chapter, is there any support you need to arrange before you begin? Write it down, and write down when you will arrange it.
Who is the person you will call if a session becomes too much? Have you told them? Do you also know how to reach professional or crisis help if needed?
What are you hoping the retreat itself will accomplish? Mark anything that belongs in the "cannot" section.
Which of the four paths are you choosing?
